scope: GDPR/PII on KDS payloads + branch isolation on KDS queries + token/role enforcement on items-board endpoint
method: read-only static analysis with adversarial lens

findings.title: GDPR data-minimization gap — customer.name still ships on all KDS payloads (Sprint 5A minimized only phone)
findings.scope_note: OWNER-DECISION V1.0.X per task brief — DO NOT HEAL in this round.
findings.consequence: Risk model: KDS endpoint requires permission:kitchen-display-system on a Sanctum-authenticated admin/staff user. Cross-tenant exposure is mitigated by Order model's BranchScope (auto-applied on Order::with(['user']) eager load — User is BranchScope-exempt for Sanctum recursion, but Order itself is scoped). So customer.name is only leaked WITHIN one branch's staff payload, which is by-design for non-DELIVERY orders the chef needs to call out (Mme Dupont's coffee). Recommendation when owner gates Yes: redact to first-name-or-initial for dine-in/takeaway/kiosk surfaces; keep full name for DELIVERY only.

findings.title: KDS items-board orderItems() relies on Order::with('orderItems') scope cascade — branch isolation is correct but not defense-in-depth
findings.consequence: Defense exists at TWO layers: (a) explicit ->where('branch_id', $userBranchId) on Order query when staff (admin bypasses with branch_id=0); (b) BranchScope auto-applied on Order AND on OrderItem (eager-load Order::with('orderItems') re-runs the OrderItem builder which has BranchScope::apply()). Both layers consistent. For admin (branch_id=0), BranchScope returns early (no filter), and the controller explicit branch filter is also skipped. Result: admin sees all branches, staff sees only theirs — correct and intentional.

red_lens_attack_attempts.attack: Manipulate ?branch_id=99 query param to force cross-branch read
red_lens_attack_attempts.blocked_by: KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService::orderItems() reads userBranchId from auth()->user(), NOT from request — request filter on branch_id is documented int-coerced in list() but NOT applied in orderItems() path. orderItems() endpoint has no client-supplied branch input — clean.

red_lens_attack_attempts.attack: Staff with branch_id=5 sends ?branch_id=0 hoping to bypass scope (admin trick)
red_lens_attack_attempts.blocked_by: userBranchId comes from auth()->user()->branch_id, not request. Request-side branch_id filter has no effect in orderItems().

red_lens_attack_attempts.attack: Soft-deleted order with stale allergens leaks to chef who shouldn't see it post-cancel
red_lens_attack_attempts.blocked_by: BranchScope + status filter on KitchenReleaseRule::itemBoardStatuses() (ACCEPT/PREPARING/PREPARED). Canceled/Delivered orders excluded.

red_lens_attack_attempts.attack: Test/dev admin@lecayenne.fr (branch_id=0) tunnels into staff-only items
red_lens_attack_attempts.blocked_by: Not an attack — admin bypass is intentional per FIX-54-8 (BranchScope:33).

findings.title: Items-board endpoint does NOT enforce idempotency or rate-limit — chef-bumping a status hits a separate endpoint that DOES, but the read-path is polling-friendly and unthrottled

evidence.route_protection: permission:kitchen-display-system middleware only — no per-IP throttle, no per-user rate limit

findings.consequence: Read endpoint, so no idempotency required. Rate-limit absent means a malicious or buggy staff client can poll at high frequency. Mitigation context: TrustProxies $proxies='*' + per-IP throttle commit 79e214542 (Wave 3 P1) likely caps egress at the global rate-limit layer. Not blocking V1, but a per-route 'kds:read' throttle (60/min) would be cheap defense.

findings.title: Allergens_snapshot is user-controlled at order creation — null/[] merge is correct, but malformed JSON in legacy rows could break json_encode in service

evidence.defense: is_array() guard + array_filter + sort + array_values + strval mapping

findings.consequence: OrderItem casts allergens_snapshot to 'array' (Models/OrderItem.php:76), so Eloquent normalizes at read. Defensive normalize() in service handles null + non-array + non-string elements. Tested by KdsAllergenAggregationSplitTest::test_items_with_NULL_allergens_snapshot_merge_with_items_with_EMPTY_array. Robust.

findings.title: Item_id leak risk in items-board response — by design, this is needed for kdsAddonDisplayName + item_name resolution
findings.evidence: items-board ships item_id + item_name + variations + extras
findings.consequence: Not PII, public-menu information. No leak.

verdict.summary: Branch isolation is sound across both layers (controller + OrderItem global scope). GDPR customer.name gap is owner-decision V1.0.X per task brief. Items-board read-endpoint has no per-route rate limit (global mitigation only). No exploitable cross-tenant leak found.
